title: Calif.io reportedly demonstrated an untethered iOS 27.0.1 jailbreak on an iPhone 18 Pro at Hexacon 2026
description: Press reports say Calif.io showed a live jailbreak of an iPhone 18 Pro running iOS 27.0.1 at Hexacon in Paris on 2026-10-16, with root access returning after a restart and no host computer involved. Hexacon 2026 itself is confirmed on the official site. The talk listing and any primary Calif.io material were not located, and nothing has been independently reproduced.
chipset_scope: A20 Pro (Apple specification for iPhone 18 Pro); demonstration chip as reported
build_scope: Not stated in the reports reviewed
limitations: Relies on press descriptions. No primary Calif.io or Hexacon talk material was found, there is no technical write-up, nothing has been independently reproduced, and the demonstration device is not the target device.

title: The reported demonstration device (iPhone 18 Pro) uses A20 Pro, so the demonstration is not direct evidence for A17 Pro
description: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro specification page lists the A20 Pro chip. The reported demonstration device is an iPhone 18 Pro. A demonstration on A20 Pro hardware therefore cannot by itself establish A17 Pro compatibility.
limitations: The chip mapping comes from Apple. The identity of the demonstration device comes from press reports.

title: iOS 27.0.1 build 24A446 is the build for iPhone16,2 (iPhone 15 Pro Max)
description: Third-party firmware indexes list build 24A446 under version 27.0.1 for device identifier iPhone16,2, released 2026-09-28. A community wiki page for the same build and device appeared in search results, and a forum thread cites the same build.
limitations: No Apple-hosted build record was located. The Apple pages checked do not list build numbers, so verification relies on third-party indexes.

title: The demonstrated jailbreak state persisted across a reboot
description: One press report says root access returned after the demonstration device was restarted on stage. Accounts of reboot behaviour differ between outlets, and no independent reproduction or video analysis has been done.
limitations: Single fetched press source. The mechanism is undisclosed and no video or independent replication was reviewed.

title: Apple's iOS 27 security notes credit Calif.io researchers for four CVE entries (CVE-2026-65409, CVE-2026-65410, CVE-2026-28968 and CVE-2026-86886)
description: Apple's iOS 27 security content page lists four CVE entries that credit Calif.io researchers, some jointly with other researchers. CVE-2026-65409 and CVE-2026-65410 credit Calif.io researchers in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research. CVE-2026-28968 carries the impact text 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or corrupt kernel memory'. CVE-2026-86886 carries the impact text 'An app may be able to modify protected system files' and the description 'A path traversal issue was addressed with improved input validation'. An entry-update note dated October 19, 2026 follows CVE-2026-28968 in the extracted text.
device_scope: Not established per entry from the extracted text; Apple's iOS 27 notes list 'iPhone 11 and later' for several entries, which would include the iPhone 15 Pro Max.
ios_scope: iOS 27 security notes; the fixed-in release per CVE is not identified in the extracted text
limitations: The extracted text does not tie each CVE to a specific 27.x release, so these entries are not shown to apply to iOS 27.0.1, and they are not shown to apply to A17 Pro.

title: Apple's iOS 27 security notes name Claude and Anthropic Research alongside Calif.io for two entries
description: Apple's text credits CVE-2026-65409 and CVE-2026-65410 to Calif.io in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research. This tracker quotes Apple's wording only. The maintainer's drafts were prepared with AI assistance from Claude, which Anthropic builds (see the disclosure in README.md). The credit does not describe the nature or extent of that collaboration.
limitations: Apple's text does not describe the collaboration. Do not infer from this entry how any jailbreak was or was not developed.

title: iOS 27.0.1 has no published CVE entries in Apple's security releases index
description: Apple's security releases index lists iOS 27.0.1 and iPadOS 27.0.1 with the note 'This update has no published CVE entries'.
device_scope: iPhone 11 and later and the iPads Apple lists for iOS 27.0.1
limitations: The note reflects Apple's published CVE entries. It does not prove that no security fixes exist, and the index extract does not show the build number.

title: iOS 27.2 (build 24B119) was released on 2026-10-26
description: Apple's security releases index lists iOS 27.2 with a 26 Oct 2026 release. ipsw.me lists build 24B119 as version 27.2 on 2026-10-26.
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (iPhone16,2) per the third-party index
limitations: The build number comes from a third-party index. Apple's index extract shows the date but not the build.

title: iOS 27.2.1 (build 24B156) was released on 2026-11-09
description: Apple's security releases index lists iOS 27.2.1 with a 09 Nov 2026 release. ipsw.me lists build 24B156 as version 27.2.1 on 2026-11-09.
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (iPhone16,2) per the third-party index
limitations: The build number comes from a third-party index. Apple's index extract shows the date but not the build.

title: iOS 27.2 fixed 163 vulnerabilities
description: Two secondary outlets report 163 vulnerabilities fixed in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2. Apple's own 27.2 advisory was not located in this check, so the count is not verified.
device_scope: Not stated in the reports reviewed
limitations: Secondary press counts only. Apple's advisory would be needed to verify the count and the components.

title: Apple says Memory Integrity Enforcement is built into all iPhone 17 and iPhone Air models and names the A19 and A19 Pro chips
description: Apple's Security Research blog says MIE is built into all iPhone 17 and iPhone Air models and that the A19 and A19 Pro chips were designed to support it. The post also says the Secure Page Table Monitor protects the kernel allocator backing store and tag storage.
chipset_scope: A19 and A19 Pro (named by Apple)
ios_scope: Not specified in the extracted text
limitations: Apple's text names the chips for the MIE hardware story. It is not a complete list of chips and says nothing explicit about A17 Pro.
notes: Launch was September 2025. The exact day was not extracted, so first_observed is the date this tracker recorded the claim.

title: A17 Pro is not among the chips Apple names for Memory Integrity Enforcement
description: The MIE post names the A19 and A19 Pro chips and does not name the A17 Pro. This is a negative inference from Apple's stated scope and is not a direct statement that A17 Pro lacks MIE hardware.
limitations: This is a negative inference from the absence of a name. Apple's full hardware documentation was not searched for the A17 Pro specifically.

title: Apple states SPTM is supported on A15-or-later and M2-or-later SoCs
description: Apple's Platform Security guide says the Secure Page Table Monitor is supported on A15 or later and M2 or later SoCs and replaces the Page Protection Layer on supported platforms.
chipset_scope: A15 or later; M2 or later
ios_scope: Not specified in the extracted text
limitations: The guide is continuously updated. The extracted text does not name the A17 Pro.

title: The A17 Pro falls within Apple's A15-or-later SPTM class
description: The A17 Pro is a later SoC than the A15, so Apple's statement covers it by ordering. The chip identity for the iPhone 15 family is supported by Wikipedia (S-030), not by an Apple specification page.
ios_scope: All iOS versions that use SPTM (Apple wording)
limitations: Depends on the chip identity (see C-026) and on Apple's ordering. No SPTM detail specific to the A17 Pro was checked.

title: A publicly disclosed SPTM bypass applies to A17 Pro on iOS 27.0.1
description: The reference repository reports a credible but undisclosed SPTM bypass that it says is valid through iOS 27.0.1. No public technical disclosure, proof of concept or independent reproduction was located, so the claim is not verified.
limitations: Community-sourced and undisclosed. No primary disclosure was found. The upstream's opa334 statement (2026-10-17) that is the main lead could not be retrieved; see C-051.

title: Dopamine 3.0 release notes state a Titan PPL/SPTM bypass for all devices on iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1
description: The Dopamine 3.0 release notes (2026-08-07) state that a Titan PPL/SPTM bypass introduces support for all devices running iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1. The notes name no chip families. A third-party table lists iOS 15.0 to 17.3.1 for A14 to A17 and M1 to M2 (S-039). That table is secondary.
device_scope: Devices running iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1 (release-note wording: all devices)
chipset_scope: Not stated in the release note. The third-party table lists A14 to A17 and M1 to M2.
limitations: Release-note statement, verified as text. The bypass method is not described. The chip table is secondary.

title: Dopamine 3.0.13 is the latest official Dopamine release (published 2026-11-03)
description: The GitHub release API lists 3.0.13 as the most recent release, published 2026-11-03. Its notes describe specific fixes and do not state iOS 27 support.
limitations: Describes the latest release only. The notes concern individual fixes rather than device support.

title: No Dopamine release is documented to support iOS 27.0.1 on A17 Pro
description: The official release notes do not mention iOS 27 support, the main README is stale, and secondary coverage lists 17.3.1 as the highest iOS version for A15 to A17 devices.
limitations: Absence of documentation. This is not a formal support statement from the project.

title: The usbliter8 BootROM exploit is reported to affect A12 and A13 chips and not A14 or later
description: Several outlets and a national CERT advisory describe a SecureROM (BootROM) flaw in A12 and A13 processors, with reports that later designs avoid it. No original researcher write-up was located, and device lists differ between outlets.
device_scope: iPhone XS, XR, 11 family and SE (2nd generation) as reported
chipset_scope: A12 and A13 (reported; S4 and S5 watch chips also reported)
limitations: Relies on secondary reporting and a CERT summary. The A14-and-later exclusion is reported, not tested here.

title: A tutorial page claims a full iOS 27 jailbreak using usbliter8
description: A tutorial-style web page claims a complete iOS 27 jailbreak chain built on usbliter8, including iBoot, SPTM, TXM and kernel patching. Its claims are unverified and the page is treated as high risk.
limitations: Unverified marketing-style claims with no evidence of working code. Not endorsed. Do not download anything from the page.

title: iOS 27.0.1 (24A446) is unsigned in the ipsw.me index on 2026-11-12, after a 2026-11-02 report that it was signed
description: The ipsw.me firmware index lists 24A446 as not signed (signed=false) when checked on 2026-11-12. The reference repository reported the build as signed on 2026-11-02 from a live index pull. Both are third-party observations. The date of the change is not known. No Apple-hosted signing record was checked.
limitations: Signing status can change. The index is a third-party status field, not an Apple statement. Do not assume that a restore to this build is possible.

title: A Calif.io-linked researcher reportedly announced a kernel read/write exploit and write-up within about a week
description: Press coverage and the reference repository both report a planned release of exploit code and a write-up about a week after 2026-11-04. A later press report says no public tool is planned. No primary announcement was located, and a 2026-11-12 check found no publication (C-049).
limitations: Conflicting secondary reports and no primary announcement. No release was located, and nothing has been reproduced.

title: An Apple CVE credit confirms the identity of the lambda handle, according to the reference repository
description: The reference repository says the lambda handle is confirmed by an Apple CVE credit (CVE-2026-112611). The iOS 27 security content page checked in this audit does not contain that identifier or the handle. This tracker does not reproduce the reference's personal-name attribution.
limitations: The CVE may appear in another Apple advisory that was not checked. The identity question concerns a private individual and is not published here.

title: iOS 27.0.1 was released on 2026-09-28
description: Apple's security releases index shows the iOS 27.0.1 entry dated 28 September 2026. ipsw.me and a community forum thread give the same release date for build 24A446.
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (iPhone16,2) via the third-party index
limitations: The Apple index extract truncated the month of the 27.0.1 date. ipsw.me supplies the full date.

title: The device identifier iPhone16,2 corresponds to the iPhone 15 Pro Max
description: ipsw.me lists device identifier iPhone16,2 under the name iPhone 15 Pro Max.
limitations: Single third-party index for the mapping. No Apple device-identifier page was checked.

title: The iPhone 15 Pro Max uses the Apple A17 Pro chip
description: Wikipedia's iPhone 15 Pro article lists the system-on-chip as Apple A17 Pro, and the task profile names the same chip for the iPhone 15 Pro Max. The Apple specification page fetched for the iPhone 15 Pro did not expose the chip name in static HTML, so it is not used as evidence here.
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (target); the cited article covers the iPhone 15 Pro
limitations: Wikipedia is a secondary source. Apple's product page did not expose the chip name in this check, and the Pro Max chip is inferred from the Pro page plus the task profile.

title: No public complete exploit chain applicable to iPhone 15 Pro Max on iOS 27.0.1 has been verified
description: The only reported complete chain was demonstrated on an iPhone 18 Pro (A20 Pro), and it has no published write-up or tool. No public chain for the A17 Pro on iOS 27.0.1 was located.
limitations: Based on absence in the searches and secondary reports. This is not a proof of absence.

title: No publicly installable jailbreak tool is verified for iOS 27.0.1 on A17 Pro
description: Calif.io's reported demonstration did not come with a public installable package, and the official Dopamine release notes do not list iOS 27 support. Downloads that advertise iOS 27.0.1 jailbreaks are not verified to relate to the demonstration.
limitations: Based on the sources reviewed. Some websites host unverified downloads and must not be trusted.

title: A GitHub account with the login pwnlambda exists
description: The GitHub users API returns a public account with the login pwnlambda, created 2014-09-11, with 27 public repositories. The account is not linked to any iOS exploit in this check.
limitations: Existence only. This does not establish any affiliation or identity, and the tracker does not attribute the handle to any named individual.

title: The latest GitHub release of the repository named Sileo/Sileo is 2.5.1 (2024-10-08), and its notes do not mention iOS 27
description: The GitHub release API returns 2.5.1 as the latest release of the repository named Sileo/Sileo, published 2024-10-08. The release notes do not contain the string 27, so they do not mention iOS 27.
ios_scope: No iOS 27 support documented in the latest release notes
limitations: Repository identity is taken from its name and was not confirmed against the project's own site. Other release channels and repository commits were not reviewed.

title: Apple states PPL and SPTM enforce execution of signed and trusted code on all platforms except macOS
description: Apple's Platform Security guide states that the Page Protection Layer and the Secure Page Table Monitor enforce execution of signed and trusted code on all platforms except macOS, and that the other security properties, including page-table protection, are present across all supported platforms.
device_scope: All Apple platforms except macOS (Apple wording)
chipset_scope: Not chip-specific in the extracted text
ios_scope: Not version-specific in the extracted text
limitations: A design statement from Apple. It does not describe bypass resistance or any specific exploit.

title: The five most recent Dopamine default-branch commit subjects do not mention iOS 27
description: The GitHub commit list for opa334/Dopamine shows five recent commits from 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-03, including the 3.0.13 release commit. Their subject lines mention hook fixes, SpringBoard snapshot handling, and detection for the iOS 26.0 beta. None mentions iOS 27.
ios_scope: iOS 26.0 beta detection mentioned; iOS 27 not mentioned in subject lines
limitations: Subject lines only. Commit bodies, branches and pull requests were not reviewed, so absence from subject lines is not proof of absence of iOS 27 work.

title: Apple's iOS 27 notes list two kernel-component entries with arbitrary code execution with kernel privileges (CVE-2026-84607 and CVE-2026-86916)
description: Apple's iOS 27 security page lists CVE-2026-84607 (AVEVideoEncoder; 'A sandboxed app may be able to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges'; description 'A race condition was addressed with improved state management.') and CVE-2026-86916 (Kernel; 'An app may be able to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges'; description 'A use after free issue was addressed with improved memory management.'). CVE-2026-86916 is marked 'Entry added October 26, 2026'. Both are on the iOS 27 (27.0) page.
device_scope: Device list not stated per entry (Apple's page lists 'iPhone 11 and later' for most entries)
chipset_scope: Not chip-specific in the extracted text
limitations: Apple's impact text is a summary. The page does not state affected version ranges. This record does not establish exploitability, or applicability to iOS 27.0.1 or the A17 Pro.

title: Apple's iOS 27 notes list eight kernel-memory read, disclosure, layout or state entries, one requiring root privileges
description: The iOS 27 page lists CVE-2026-84622 (Kernel; 'An app with root privileges may be able to read uninitialized kernel memory'), CVE-2026-65359 (Kernel; 'A local user may be able to cause unexpected system termination or read kernel memory'), CVE-2026-65415 (Kernel; the same impact), CVE-2026-86903 and CVE-2026-84530 (Kernel; 'An app may be able to disclose kernel memory'), CVE-2026-43687 (Kernel; 'Connecting to a malicious NFS server may disclose kernel memory'), CVE-2026-65405 (Kernel; 'An app may be able to determine kernel memory layout') and CVE-2026-64760 (IOSurfaceAccelerator; 'An app may be able to leak sensitive kernel state').
chipset_scope: Not chip-specific in the extracted text
limitations: Impact text as published by Apple. These are not classified here as usable kernel read primitives for the target. No exploit or reproduction was reviewed.

title: Apple's iOS 27 notes list a kernel entry that lets a malicious app gain root privileges (CVE-2026-43689)
description: CVE-2026-43689 (component Kernel) carries the impact 'A malicious app may be able to gain root privileges' and the description 'A permissions issue was addressed with additional restrictions.' It appears in the iOS 27 notes (27.0 release).
limitations: Impact text only. The affected version range and the code path are not stated.

title: Apple's iOS 27 notes list kernel-memory write and corruption entries, including the Calif.io-credited CVE-2026-28968
description: Write entries: CVE-2026-84523 (APFS) and CVE-2026-84634 (Apple Neural Engine), both 'unexpected system termination or write kernel memory'. Corruption entries: CVE-2026-28968 (Kernel; Calif.io-credited; 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or corrupt kernel memory'), CVE-2026-65398 (IOMobileFrameBuffer; the same impact), CVE-2026-84507, CVE-2026-84561 and CVE-2026-84599 (Kernel; the same impact), CVE-2026-84566 (Kernel; 'A local attacker may be able to cause unexpected system termination or corrupt kernel memory') and CVE-2026-43686 (Kernel; 'Connecting to a malicious NFS server may lead to kernel memory corruption'). The page lists 2 write and 7 corruption entries for iOS 27. CVE-2026-28968 carries an 'Entry updated October 19, 2026' note.
limitations: Apple's impact text only. The fixed-in release of each entry is not stated in the extracted text.

title: Apple's iOS 27 notes credit Calif.io for four entries with different components and impacts
description: The iOS 27 page credits Calif.io on CVE-2026-65409 (Foundation; 'An app may be able to cause a denial of service'), CVE-2026-65410 (AVEVideoEncoder; 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination'), CVE-2026-28968 (Kernel; 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or corrupt kernel memory') and CVE-2026-86886 (TCC; 'An app may be able to modify protected system files'). Of these, only CVE-2026-28968 has a kernel-memory impact.
limitations: Credits as printed by Apple. Individual names are not reproduced in this repository.

title: Apple's iOS 27.2 notes list 23 kernel-memory entries (4 write, 12 corruption, 1 copy-on-write, 6 read or disclosure) and no kernel or root privilege entry
description: The iOS 27.2 page lists 15 identifiers under the Kernel component and 23 identifiers with a kernel-memory impact. Write impacts: CVE-2026-112474, CVE-2026-112507, CVE-2026-84494, CVE-2026-84495. Corruption impacts: CVE-2026-112459, CVE-2026-112468, CVE-2026-112469, CVE-2026-112470, CVE-2026-112477, CVE-2026-112514, CVE-2026-112517, CVE-2026-112679, CVE-2026-112689, CVE-2026-112696, CVE-2026-65350, CVE-2026-86969. Copy-on-write: CVE-2026-112576. Most entries have device list 'iPhone 11 and later'. The page does not state an affected iOS version.
device_scope: iPhone 11 and later for the entries reviewed (Apple device lists)
ios_scope: iOS 27.2 notes (27.2 release, 2026-10-26); affected versions not stated
limitations: Apple's impact text only. Affected version ranges are not stated, so this record does not show whether iOS 27.0.1 was affected. Read-only and termination-only entries are in C-040 and C-041.

title: Apple's iOS 27.2 notes list six kernel-memory read, disclosure or layout entries from several components
description: CVE-2026-112466 (AVEVideoEncoder; 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or read kernel memory'), CVE-2026-112479 (USB; 'A malicious USB device may be able to cause unexpected system termination or read kernel memory'), CVE-2026-112515 (IOHIDFamily; 'An attacker may be able to cause unexpected system termination or read kernel memory'), CVE-2026-112554 (IOStorageFamily; 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or read kernel memory'), CVE-2026-113910 (Compression; 'An app may be able to disclose kernel memory') and CVE-2026-112665 (Kernel; 'An app may be able to determine kernel memory layout').
limitations: Impact text only. Read and disclosure primitives are not classified here as usable for the target. No public technical analysis was found for these entries.

title: Apple's iOS 27.2 notes list further kernel-memory corruption and write entries in Apple Neural Engine and AVEVideoEncoder
description: Apple Neural Engine: CVE-2026-112696 ('An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or corrupt kernel memory') and CVE-2026-84494 ('An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or write kernel memory'). AVEVideoEncoder: CVE-2026-112468, CVE-2026-112469, CVE-2026-112470 and CVE-2026-112689, each 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination or corrupt kernel memory'.
limitations: Impact text only; affected versions not stated.

title: The six Calif.io-credited entries in Apple's iOS 27.2 notes carry no kernel read or write impact
description: Apple's iOS 27.2 notes credit Calif.io on six identifiers: CVE-2026-112611 (CoreGraphics; 'Processing a maliciously crafted PDF file may lead to memory corruption'), CVE-2026-112684 (WebKit; 'Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected process crash'), CVE-2026-112692 (App Intents; 'An app may be able to access sensitive user data'), CVE-2026-112705 (AVEVideoEncoder; 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination'), CVE-2026-113912 (CoreAudio; 'Processing a maliciously crafted media file may lead to unexpected app termination or corrupt process memory') and CVE-2026-113950 (CoreGraphics; font processing, 'unexpected app termination or corrupt process memory'). None of these impacts is kernel memory. The script-computed check found no kernel-memory impact among them.
device_scope: iPhone 11 and later (Apple device list for the entries extracted)
limitations: The upstream reference describes CVE-2026-112705 as kernel-level (see C-044). Credits are recorded by organisation only.

title: CVE-2026-112611 and CVE-2026-113912 credit a Calif.io-affiliated researcher by handle, but neither is a kernel entry
description: Apple's iOS 27.2 notes credit a Calif.io-affiliated researcher by the handle @pwnlambda on CVE-2026-112611 (CoreGraphics; 'Processing a maliciously crafted PDF file may lead to memory corruption') and on CVE-2026-113912 (CoreAudio; 'Processing a maliciously crafted media file may lead to unexpected app termination or corrupt process memory'). The researcher's name is printed on Apple's page and is not reproduced here.
limitations: These entries do not establish kernel read/write. They are kept separate from the announced kernel read/write work (see C-022 and C-049).

title: Apple's entry for CVE-2026-112705 lists the AVEVideoEncoder component with an impact of unexpected system termination, not a kernel-level impact
description: The iOS 27.2 notes list CVE-2026-112705 (component AVEVideoEncoder; 'An app may be able to cause unexpected system termination'; description 'An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved bounds checking'), with credits to Calif.io researchers. The upstream reference describes the same component as kernel-level.
limitations: Apple does not state whether the AVEVideoEncoder code path runs in the kernel. This record compares only the impact text with the upstream label.

title: Apple's iOS 27.2.1 notes list nine CVE identifiers, none of them one of the six target kernel entries
description: The iOS 27.2.1 advisory (released 2026-11-09) lists nine identifiers. CVE-2026-111497 (brotli; 'Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption'); CVE-2026-113960 and CVE-2026-113961 (Messages); CVE-2026-113963 (App Intents; access to sensitive user data); CVE-2026-113964 and CVE-2026-113965 (CoreUtils; pairing and rate limits); CVE-2026-113968 (AirPlay) and CVE-2026-113969 (rapportd), both rate-limit issues; CVE-2026-113970 (Bluetooth; 'An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory'). None is listed under the Kernel component.
device_scope: Per Apple's device lists (not extracted per entry)
limitations: Component and impact of the nine entries were not mapped in this pass.

title: Apple's iOS 27.2 notes contain 162 distinct CVE identifiers in the extracted text; press reports 163
description: A text extraction of Apple's iOS 27.2 security page yields 162 distinct CVE identifiers. Press coverage reports 163 vulnerabilities fixed in iOS 27.2. The difference is not explained by the extraction method used here.
limitations: Counting method: distinct CVE identifiers in the extracted text. The press count may use a different basis.

title: Apple's iOS 27.2 notes state no affected iOS versions for the listed entries
description: The iOS 27.2 page does not state an affected iOS version for any entry. The word 'affect' does not appear in its text. Entries are listed as fixed in the release, with component, impact, description and credits.
limitations: Describes the advisory format as parsed. Apple's other documentation was not searched for version ranges.

title: Apple's iOS 27.2 notes list a WebContent sandbox-escape entry that a remote attacker may use (CVE-2026-112690)
description: CVE-2026-112690 is listed under the App Store component, for iPhone 11 and later, with the impact 'A remote attacker may be able to break out of the WebContent sandbox' and the description 'This issue was addressed with improved input validation.' It is fixed in iOS 27.2 per the advisory. A second entry, CVE-2026-113897 (WebKit Process Model; 'A remote attacker may be able to break out of Web Content sandbox'), is also listed on the 27.2 page.
limitations: Impact text only. The component label is not used here. Applicability to iOS 27.0.1 is not established.

title: No public kernel read/write write-up or exploit code by the researcher announced on 2026-11-04 was found as of 2026-11-12
description: Searches and a GitHub account check on 2026-11-12 found no write-up, release or repository for the kernel read/write work announced on 2026-11-04. The researcher's public GitHub account showed 27 public repositories on the first API page (sorted by creation date). The newest was created 2026-01-17 and has no description. No repository name contains kernel, KRW, exploit or jailbreak terms. Contents were not reviewed.
ios_scope: Not stated (the announcement did not name a version)
limitations: Negative search result. Absence from search and from one account is not proof that nothing was published elsewhere.

title: opa334 is reported (2026-11-04) to plan A12/A13 Dopamine support via momentarius once a kernel read/write exploit is public, with A14 and later still needing an SPTM bypass
description: The upstream reference (V31) reports, from Chinese-language reprints of an infosec.exchange post, that opa334 said A12 and A13 support could follow quickly using momentarius, and that A14 and later devices would still need an n-day SPTM bypass. The original post was not retrieved.
device_scope: A12 and A13 (as reported); A14 and later (as reported)
chipset_scope: A12, A13, A14 and later (as reported)
limitations: Reported second-hand by the upstream reference. The original post was not retrieved.

title: A 2026-10-17 opa334 statement is reported to warn of an SPTM bypass valid through iOS 27.0.1 (upstream V7)
description: The upstream reference reports an opa334 PSA dated 2026-10-17 warning of an SPTM bypass valid through iOS 27.0.1, reportedly confirmed as real by another researcher, and reportedly patched in a 27.2 beta. The original PSA was not located by search or fetch in this review. Its kernel-coverage statement (V8) is treated separately in C-054.
limitations: Second-hand. Original not retrieved. Bypass details are not public.

title: A Calif.io researcher is reported to have said the jailbreak applies to any iPhone running iOS 27.0.1, possibly including iPads (upstream V10)
description: The upstream reference attributes to a Calif.io team member a statement that the jailbreak applies to any iPhone running iOS 27.0.1, possibly including iPads, from an interview it dates to 2026-10-19. The English and German heise pages and the t3n page, saved on 2026-11-12, do not quote the statement. The interview itself was not retrieved. The upstream lists the claim as verified on the strength of that interview, which this review did not see.
chipset_scope: Not stated (A14 PPL scope not established)
limitations: Interview not located. The statement's scope (A14 PPL, iPadOS) is not established.

title: A Calif.io video is reported to show a jailbreak state surviving an over-the-air update to iOS 27.2 with Lockdown Mode enabled (upstream V32)
description: The upstream reference reports a 2026-11-04 Calif.io video in which Lockdown Mode is enabled, the device is updated over the air to iOS 27.2, and a plugin still works after reboot. The mechanism is undisclosed. The video and original post were not retrieved in this review.
limitations: Second-hand. The upstream reports that the over-the-air segment of the video was edited, and that a team member said a full uncut version could be shared. Neither the video nor the original post was retrieved.

title: The upstream states that DarkSword and ClearSword kernel exploits support iOS only up to 26.0.1 (V8); no primary source confirms the range
description: The upstream reference (V8) states that the existing ClearSword and DarkSword kernel exploits support only iOS up to 26.0.1. The Dopamine 3.0 release notes name both exploits and a DarkSword or ClearSword workaround, but state no version range for either (C-068). An analysis dated 2026-05-03 covers DarkSword only and gives Apple's fixed-in versions as 26.2 (CVE-2025-43510) and 26.3 (CVE-2025-43520) (C-069). The upstream range describes exploit support. That may differ from the exposure of the underlying bug. The two statements are not reconciled.
chipset_scope: Not stated (the analysis cites pre-A15 devices for 18.x)
limitations: No primary Dopamine statement of the ClearSword or DarkSword version range was found in the release notes. The 8kSec analysis covers DarkSword only.

title: No Dopamine 3.0.x release note from 3.0.2 to 3.0.13 mentions iOS 27 support
description: The GitHub release notes for Dopamine 3.0.2 to 3.0.13 (published 2026-08-09 to 2026-11-03) do not mention iOS 27 support. The base release 3.0 (2026-08-07) mentions iOS 27.0 betas only for virtual-device (Corellium) testing and limits real-device support to iOS 17.3.1 (C-066).
limitations: Release notes only. Commit bodies and other branches were not reviewed. Absence from the notes is not proof of unsupported behaviour.

title: The repository formerly at evelyneee/ellekit redirects to tealbathingsuit/ellekit, which has no GitHub release
description: The GitHub API reports that the former evelyneee/ellekit identifier (repository ID 559919558) redirects to tealbathingsuit/ellekit, the repository with that identifier. The destination has no GitHub release (checked 2026-11-12) and was last pushed on 2026-07-31.
limitations: The relation of this repository to the ElleKit project named in other sources is not confirmed by a project statement.

title: ElleKit 1.2 is reported to cover iOS 15 to 27 (upstream reference)
description: The upstream reference reports that ElleKit 1.2 (2026-07-31) covers rootless injection on iOS 15 to 27 (arm64). It cites a single secondary article. The candidate repository has no GitHub release record. Its last push date (2026-07-31) matches the reported date, but does not establish a version.
limitations: Release record not found. The statement is not verified.

title: A public GitHub repository named staturnzz/momentarius is described as an A12/A13 PPL bypass
description: The GitHub repository staturnzz/momentarius was created 2026-08-07, last pushed 2026-08-07 and updated 2026-11-05. Its description reads 'A12/A13 PPL Bypass'. Only repository metadata was retrieved (MIT licence, not archived, not a fork). Dopamine 3.0 release notes describe the same bypass (C-067). The code was not downloaded, reviewed or run.
limitations: Metadata only. The description is the repository's own statement and is not verified. This record makes no claim about the code.

title: An independent SPTM analysis states that SPTM replaced PPL on A15 or newer and M2 or newer SoCs
description: arXiv paper 2510.09272 (submitted 2025-10-10; 'Modern iOS Security Features: A Deep Dive into SPTM, TXM, and Exclaves') states that SPTM and TXM were released for A15/M2 or newer SoCs in 2023 and that SPTM has replaced the PPL mitigation on A15 and M2 or newer SoCs.
device_scope: Devices with A15 or newer SoCs (per the paper)
chipset_scope: A15 or newer; M2 or newer
limitations: Independent analysis. Its firmware work used other hardware (see C-060).

title: The arXiv SPTM analysis's firmware work uses an iPhone 16 on iOS 18.4. The paper does not analyse the A17 Pro or any iOS 27 build
description: The arXiv paper states that its main firmware analysis used iOS 18.4 (22E240) firmware for the iPhone 16, and that a research device ran iOS 18.5. A full-text search on 2026-11-12 found no mention of A16, A17, A18, A19 or A20 beyond the A15 SPTM statement (C-059), and no mention of iOS 26, iOS 27, iPhone 15 or iPhone 17. The paper does not name the iPhone 16's SoC in the text.
device_scope: iPhone 16 (A18) in the paper's firmware analysis
chipset_scope: A18 in the paper's firmware analysis
limitations: Full-text search of the HTML version of the paper (v1). Figures and appendices were not reviewed one by one.

title: Press coverage reports that AI helped build the Calif.io jailbreak (not confirmed by the team)
description: heise's headline states that AI helped create the iOS 27.0.1 jailbreak, and t3n reports that AI was used to locate the exploit chain. The Calif.io team has not published its method, and the coverage reviewed does not name the models used.
chipset_scope: A20 Pro (as reported for that model)
limitations: Press claims. No team statement located. The coverage's AI claims are not verified.

title: A third party is reported to have reproduced CVE-2026-112705 as a crash on iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.0.1 (unverified)
description: The upstream reference (V17) reports that a third party independently reproduced CVE-2026-112705 on an iPhone 17 Pro running iOS 27.0.1 and published a proof of concept. The reported effect is a kernel-side out-of-bounds write that causes a panic, which the upstream describes as denial-of-service class, without arbitrary read or write. No exploit detail is recorded here.
device_scope: iPhone 17 Pro (as reported; not the target)
limitations: Reported by the upstream reference, which states that the repository exists. This review did not visit, download or run it, and no link is recorded. Apple's impact text for CVE-2026-112705 is 'unexpected system termination' (C-044). The report does not establish any read or write capability.

title: A company-branded account is reported to have shown a root shell on iOS 27.2 (unverified)
description: The upstream reference (V18) reports that a company-branded account demonstrated on 2026-10-30 a global icon change and a root shell on iOS 27.2. It reports no CVE, no disclosure commitment and no independent media confirmation.
limitations: Single-party evidence (image or video). Device model and method are not stated. If it were true, it would describe a route other than the one reported for the Calif.io demonstration. This is not established.

title: A project announced on 2026-11-01 claims a semi-untethered iOS 27.0 to 27.0.1 jailbreak for iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro); no release or validation was located
description: The upstream reference (V21, V22, V28) reports a project announced on 2026-11-01 for iOS 27.0 to 27.0.1, described as semi-untethered, with a planned release one to two weeks later. The project reportedly names iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro) as its only test device. The reported status is that its kernel-level stage works and that a later stage is unfinished. The upstream found no proof of concept or third-party validation, and rates the claims unverifiable. This record treats any future release as potentially malicious and does not link to any project resource.
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro), as reported as the only test device
limitations: Self-reported claims, recorded second-hand. The individual behind the project is not named here. No release, code or third-party validation was reviewed. No stage is mapped to any listed CVE (see C-042, C-073). The claim, if real, would still need the exact-target verification that this project requires (LEVEL 5).

title: Dopamine 3.0 release notes state a Titan PPL/SPTM bypass for all devices on iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1
description: The Dopamine 3.0 release notes (published 2026-08-07) state that a Titan PPL/SPTM bypass introduces support for all devices running iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1. The notes name the bypass's developer but do not describe its method.
device_scope: Devices running iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1 (release-note wording: all devices)
limitations: Release-note statement, verified as text. The release notes do not name chip families. It does not cover iOS 27.

title: Dopamine 3.0 release notes say real-device SPTM support stops at iOS 17.3.1 because no SPTM bypass is known for iOS 17.4 and later
description: The Dopamine 3.0 release notes (2026-08-07) say that support for SPTM devices up to the 27.0 betas has been added in general, that it can be tested on Corellium virtual devices, and that it 'obviously only works up to 17.3.1 on real devices due to lack of an SPTM bypass on >=17.4'.
device_scope: Real SPTM devices (release-note wording); virtual devices for iOS 27 betas
ios_scope: iOS 17.4 and later (no bypass per the notes); iOS 27 betas on virtual devices only
limitations: The statement is the project's, dated 2026-08-07. It predates the October 2026 reports of a further SPTM bypass (C-051), and the project may have changed its view since. It concerns Dopamine's support, not SPTM in general.

title: Dopamine 3.0 release notes describe a momentarius PPL bypass for A12 and A13 devices on iOS 16.6 to 18.7.1 and 26.0 to 26.0.1
description: The Dopamine 3.0 release notes (2026-08-07) state that a momentarius PPL bypass, by the project's listed developers, introduces support for A12 and A13 devices running iOS 16.6 to 18.7.1 and 26.0 to 26.0.1.
limitations: Release-note statement. The repository metadata (C-058) is consistent with it. The code was not reviewed. Not applicable to the A17 Pro.

title: Dopamine 3.0 release notes name ClearSword and DarkSword workarounds but state no iOS version range for either exploit
description: The Dopamine 3.0 release notes (2026-08-07) name a ClearSword exploit, described as a cleaner alternative to DarkSword, and a DarkSword or ClearSword respring workaround for A8 devices. The notes give no iOS version range for either exploit.
device_scope: A8 devices for the workaround (release-note wording)
limitations: Release-note text only. Other release notes and commit history were not reviewed. This record is the basis for C-054's 'unverified' verdict.

title: 8kSec reports Apple's fixed-in versions for the two DarkSword kernel CVEs as iOS 26.2 and 26.3 (secondary analysis)
description: A security-company analysis dated 2026-05-03 reports that Apple's advisories fix CVE-2025-43510 in iOS 18.7.5 and 26.2, and CVE-2025-43520 in iOS 18.7.6 and 26.3.
device_scope: Not applicable (kernel bugs; the analysis cites pre-A15 devices for the 18.x fixes)
ios_scope: iOS 18.7.5 to 18.7.6 and 26.2 to 26.3 (fixed-in versions, as reported)
limitations: Apple's 26.x advisories were not retrieved. The version data comes from a secondary analysis.

title: Apple's iOS 27 notes list CVE-2026-112608 (CoreMedia) as added on 2026-10-26
description: Apple's iOS 27 security page lists CVE-2026-112608 under CoreMedia, with the impact 'Processing a maliciously crafted Bluetooth packet may result in disclosure of process memory' and the description 'An out-of-bounds read was addressed with improved bounds checking.' The entry is marked 'Entry added October 26, 2026'.
device_scope: Apple device list not checked for this entry
limitations: Apple's impact text. Not kernel memory in Apple's wording. Affected version ranges are not stated.

title: Apple's iOS 27 page marks 45 identifiers as added or updated on 2026-10-19 or 2026-10-26
description: Apple's iOS 27 security page marks 45 identifiers with 'Entry added' or 'Entry updated' notes dated October 19 or October 26, 2026. The page lists these entries under iOS 27 and states no affected version range.
limitations: The notes give the date an entry was added or updated on the page. They do not give the date a fix shipped in a given build, so 'fixed in 27.0' means listed on the 27.0 page.

title: Most Apple entries in iOS 27 and 27.2 apply to iPhone 11 and later; three Apple Intelligence entries apply to iPhone 15 Pro and later
description: Apple's iOS 27 and iOS 27.2 security pages list most entries for 'iPhone 11 and later'. The Apple Intelligence entries CVE-2026-86920 and CVE-2026-86955 (iOS 27) and CVE-2026-86987 (iOS 27.2) list 'iPhone 15 Pro and later', which on its face includes the iPhone 15 Pro Max.
device_scope: iPhone 11 and later; iPhone 15 Pro and later (Apple device lists)
limitations: A device list is Apple's statement of applicability. It does not show that the entry is reachable on a given device. The Apple Intelligence entries describe access to user data, not kernel memory.

title: Apple's iOS 27 and iOS 27.2 notes do not mention AGX, IOGPU, SPTM, TXM, PPL, CoreTrust, AMFI or Exclave
description: A text search of the extracted iOS 27 and iOS 27.2 security pages (2026-11-12) found none of the terms AGX, IOGPU, SPTM, TXM, PPL, CoreTrust, AMFI or Exclave.
limitations: A term search of the extracted text. Apple's notes name components and impacts only. Absence of a term does not show that a component is unaffected.

title: Apple's iOS 27 notes list four kernel or root privilege entries; the iOS 27.2 notes list none
description: The iOS 27 page lists four entries with kernel or root privilege impacts: CVE-2026-43689 ('A malicious app may be able to gain root privileges'), CVE-2026-84607 and CVE-2026-86916 ('execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges'), and CVE-2026-84622 ('An app with root privileges may be able to read uninitialized kernel memory'). The iOS 27.2 page lists none.
ios_scope: iOS 27 (27.0 page); none on iOS 27.2 page
limitations: Apple's impact text. No exploit or chain is implied. Affected version ranges are not stated.

title: heise reports the Calif.io jailbreak as 'the first reboot-proof jailbreak since iOS 9' (press claim; unverified)
description: heise (English edition, 2026-10-16) states that the Calif.io team 'has developed the first reboot-proof jailbreak since iOS 9'. The upstream reference (E1) reports that a public untethered jailbreak for iOS 14.3 to 14.5.1 from 2021 contradicts that framing. This record keeps the press wording and does not adopt either framing.
ios_scope: iOS 27.0.1 and earlier iOS 9 comparison (as reported)
limitations: The 2021 comparison is the upstream's and is not verified here.

title: t3n reports AI-assisted exploit-chain discovery and an iOS 27.2 beta comparison as established; heise calls the comparison theoretical
description: t3n (2026-10-18) reports that Calif.io used AI to find the exploit chain and that the team compared the iOS 27.2 beta with iOS 27.0.1 with AI support to identify the security fixes. heise (German edition, 2026-10-16) describes the comparison as theoretically possible. No team statement on the method was located.
limitations: Press claims. The AI models used were not named by the team. The coverage reviewed does not show the method.

title: The upstream reports a Calif.io team member saying the team will not release an end-user jailbreak tool (unverified)
description: The upstream reference reports that a Calif.io team member said in a 2026-10-19 interview that the team does not plan an end-user jailbreak tool, may disclose vulnerabilities so that third parties can build tools, and might release a proof of concept after Apple's fix. The interview was not retrieved.
limitations: Second-hand. The upstream classifies this as verified from the interview. That interview was not seen here.

title: The 24A446 manifest's KernelCache digest equals the SHA-384 of the raw IM4P container (identities 0, 1 and 2)
description: The BuildManifest entry for the kernelcache (path kernelcache.release.iphone16) carries a 48-byte digest. Its SHA-384 equals the SHA-384 of the raw IM4P container retrieved from the package. The digest is identical in all three build identities.
limitations: Checked on the retrieved container. The complete package was not hashed. The restore-entry digest is a separate claim (C-080).

title: The analysed 24A446 kernelcache is the LZFSE decompression of the verified container (73,023,488 bytes, byte-identical)
description: The IM4P metadata reports LZFSE compression, an uncompressed size of 73,023,488 bytes and no key bag. Decompression with the ipsw tool gives output byte-identical to the kernelcache used for analysis.
limitations: Decompression was performed by one tool. An independent decoder was not used for a cross-check.

title: Restore-entry digests for the 24A446 kernelcache and the SPTM and TXM monitors do not match the retrieved containers
description: The manifest entries RestoreKernelCache, Ap,RestoreSecurePageTableMonitor and Ap,RestoreTrustedExecutionMonitor carry digests that differ from the SHA-384 of the containers retrieved at the same archive paths.
limitations: The mismatch is verified. Its cause is unresolved. The restore-variant objects were not retrieved, so no conclusion is drawn about them.

title: The 24A446 package contains SPTM and TXM monitor containers that are unencrypted, with matching normal manifest digests
description: The sptm and trxm IM4P containers carry no key bag, use LZFSE compression, and have SHA-384 digests equal to their normal manifest entries (Ap,SecurePageTableMonitor and Ap,TrustedExecutionMonitor). Both decompress to Mach-O MH_EXECUTE files.
limitations: Verified for the containers and payload structure. The code inside the monitors is not interpreted by this record.

title: The 24A446 kernelcache fileset contains the sandbox, AMFI, CoreTrust and Image4 bundles, by exact identifier
description: The bundle identifiers com.apple.security.sandbox, com.apple.driver.AppleMobileFileIntegrity, com.apple.kext.CoreTrust, com.apple.security.AppleImage4 and com.apple.security.Image4 are present in the kernelcache fileset.
limitations: Presence of a component on the build. This is not evidence that the component is affected by any advisory or reachable, and it does not establish applicability (C-047).

title: The 24A446 kernelcache contains kernel log strings that name SPTM and TXM interfaces
description: Defined strings in the kernelcache refer to the SPTM version and load address, ASIDs supplied by SPTM, and TXM load address and thread associations.
limitations: Presence of strings only. The behaviour of the code paths that use them was not analysed.

title: The 24A446 kernelcache contains MIE-related strings; whether MIE is active on the A17 Pro is not established
description: The kernelcache contains the strings 'MIE factor' and 'MIE update', and an MTE soft-mode message for ptraced processes.
limitations: Presence is verified. Activation on the A17 Pro is not established. Apple names MIE for A19 and later (C-011, C-012).

title: Ghidra recorded no code reference into the 24A446 __DATA_SPTM segment; the cause is unresolved
description: The __DATA_SPTM segment is a single read-only block. Every address in it was checked, and the only recorded reference comes from the linkage segment, not from code.
limitations: A limitation of one automatic analysis (17 logged errors). Possible causes are unresolved accesses, access from the monitor side, or the analysis errors. It is not a finding about the segment's behaviour.

title: Standalone KEXT files extracted from the 24A446 kernelcache have empty symbol tables, and Ghidra cannot import them
description: Each of the eight standalone bundles has LC_SYMTAB with zero symbols and an 8-byte string table. Ghidra's Mach-O loader fails on each file, whether or not imports were resolved.
limitations: The cause, whether the extraction or the loader, is not established. Analysis used the kernelcache fileset instead.

title: Ghidra's automatic analysis of the 24A446 kernelcache completed, recovering 230,298 functions (3 named) with 17 logged errors
description: The analysis completed and the program was saved. Of the recovered functions, 230,295 have default names. The log records 13 function-creation failures caused by thunk overlaps and 4 value-tracking failures.
limitations: The completion and the counts are tool outputs. The errors leave some regions unanalysed, and original symbol names are essentially absent.

title: Ghidra's automatic analysis of the 24A446 TXM image completed without logged errors, recovering 1,654 functions (1,653 default-named)
description: The TXM image (an IM4P of type trxm, decompressed to a six-segment Mach-O) was imported and analysed. Analysis succeeded, the program was saved, and no analyser errors were logged. The program has 1,654 functions, 1,653 of them default-named, and 21 memory blocks.
limitations: Tool output. Original function names are essentially absent, and the counts include analysis-generated functions. The behaviour of the TXM code was not reviewed.

title: The 24B119 (27.2) manifest's KernelCache, SPTM and TXM normal digests match the retrieved containers
description: In the first build identity, the BuildManifest digests for the kernelcache, SPTM and TXM equal the SHA-384 of the containers retrieved by range request.
limitations: Retrieved containers only. The complete package was not hashed.

title: The 24B119 (27.2) restore-entry digests for the kernelcache, SPTM and TXM do not match the retrieved containers
description: The restore entries for the kernelcache, SPTM and TXM carry digests that differ from the SHA-384 of the containers retrieved at the same archive paths.
limitations: The mismatch is verified. Its cause is unresolved. Restore-variant objects were not retrieved.

title: The 24B156 (27.2.1) manifest's KernelCache, SPTM and TXM normal digests match the retrieved containers
description: In the first build identity, the BuildManifest digests for the kernelcache, SPTM and TXM equal the SHA-384 of the containers retrieved by range request.
limitations: Retrieved containers only. The complete package was not hashed.

title: The 24B156 (27.2.1) restore-entry digests for the kernelcache, SPTM and TXM do not match the retrieved containers
description: The restore entries for the kernelcache, SPTM and TXM carry digests that differ from the SHA-384 of the containers retrieved at the same archive paths.
limitations: The mismatch is verified. Its cause is unresolved. Restore-variant objects were not retrieved.

title: The SPTM and TXM containers of 24B119 and 24B156 are byte-identical to each other and differ from 24A446
description: The SPTM and TXM IM4P containers have the same SHA-256 in 27.2 and 27.2.1, and both differ from the 27.0.1 containers. Their decompressed sizes are the same in all three builds.
limitations: Byte identity of the containers only. What the monitor code does is not compared (no code-level comparison was made).

title: The kernel version strings are darwin 27.0.0 (XNU 13432.2.10~2) for 24A446 and darwin 27.2.0 (XNU 13432.42.3~28) for 24B119 and 24B156
description: The version record inside each decompressed kernelcache reports these darwin and XNU strings. Both 27.2 builds report the same strings.
chipset_scope: T8122 (kernel CPU field; not mapped to the A17 Pro by any cited source)
limitations: Version strings only. They do not establish which changes a build contains.

title: The KEXT inventories of 24B119 and 24B156 contain the same 281 records as 24A446; 47 bundle-version and 48 short-version fields differ from 24A446 in each
description: No KEXT record is added or removed between 24A446 and either 27.2 build. The two 27.2 builds have identical version fields.
limitations: Counts from the ipsw KEXT listing. A version change is not treated as a security fix, and no version change is interpreted here. The two version fields differ because the bundle-version field and the short-version field change independently for one record.

title: The kernelcache and the SPTM and TXM monitor images of 24A446 carry the arm64e subtype bit in their Mach-O headers
description: The subtype field of each Mach-O header has the arm64e bit set. The images are therefore built for pointer-authentication-capable code.
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
chipset_scope: A17 Pro target family (arm64e build flag)
limitations: A build-level header flag. It does not show that pointer authentication is enforced on any device.

title: The signature set kernel/27.0 in the symbolicator repository declares a darwin range of 27.0.0 to 27.2.0
description: The xnu signature file declares a minimum darwin version of 27.0.0 and a maximum of 27.2.0, and its KEXT signature files all declare ranges that include 27.0.0.
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
limitations: The declared range is the repository's own statement. The signatures' accuracy is not established by this claim.

title: About 80% of the distinct xnu signature anchor strings occur in the 24A446 kernelcache
description: Of 14,189 distinct anchor strings in the xnu signature file, 11,317 are present in the 24A446 kernelcache (79.8%). Of the 6,003 signatures that carry anchors, 4,714 have all anchors present.
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
limitations: Presence of the strings only. A string present in the binary does not show that the signature matches the function it names.

title: Signature-assisted symbolication of the 24A446 kernel assigns non-equivalent names to 1,139 addresses
description: Logged output gives 1,160 kernel addresses with more than one signature name. For 1,139 of them the names belong to different families after normalising constructor, destructor and cold-split variants.
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
limitations: Some pairs may be true aliases that the normalisation does not capture. The correct name at each address is not established.

title: On 58 kernel addresses that have independent table-derived names, signature names agree in 55 (94.8%)
description: The comparison uses syscall-table and Mach-trap-table names at the same addresses. The 95% interval is 85.9% to 98.2%.
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
limitations: A small sample, biased toward functions the signatures found. The rate does not establish accuracy for other names.

title: Ghidra cannot import the standalone KEXT files extracted from the 24A446 kernelcache, because stub processing reads symbols from an empty table
description: The failure is raised while the loader processes stub entries that point at symbol index 0, and the symbol table of each standalone file has no entries. Copying a standalone file with its indirect-symbol count set to zero imports successfully. The release kernelcache's own symbol tables are empty, and the standalone files carry the same symbol and indirect-symbol counts as their fileset entries (their string table is larger).
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
limitations: Tested with one Ghidra version. Why the fileset load does not raise the same exception was not traced. Extends C-086 with the mechanism.

title: Of the 281 KEXT inventory records of 24A446, 263 match a fileset entry, 11 are codeless and 7 are kernel-programming-interface pseudo-KEXTs with no fileset entry
description: No alias or duplicate record was found. The one fileset entry without an inventory record is the kernel image itself.
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
limitations: Records outside the fileset are not treated as missing firmware components. Their absence from the fileset is expected for codeless and interface bundles.

title: Ghidra's reference model records no register-indirect call references in the 24A446 SPTM or TXM images, while a byte-level decoder finds such encodings in both
description: Ghidra records zero indirect call and jump references for both monitor programs. The decoder finds 83 register-indirect call encodings in the SPTM and 279 in the TXM.
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
limitations: The two methods disagree and the disagreement is not resolved. The decoder counts upper bounds.

title: Four methods found no code path that addresses the 24A446 __DATA_SPTM segment; the cause of the absence is unresolved
description: A reference scan with Ghidra, a PC-relative (ADRP) pair scan, a literal-load scan and a MOVZ/MOVK constant scan found no reference to the segment. One raw 8-byte value in the segment's range lies in a __TEXT segment and is loaded by no decoded literal instruction. Extends C-085.
device_scope: Not device-specific (kernel analysis of iPhone16,2 build 24A446)
limitations: Absence by these four methods is not evidence that the segment is unused. Accesses through other encodings, through the SPTM side or through the interface were not tested.

title: Apple's Platform Security guide states that SPTM is supported on A15-or-later and M2-or-later SoCs, and that SPTM with TXM replaces the PPL there
description: The OS-integrity section of the guide, re-read on 2026-11-12, gives the SPTM support statement and the replacement statement. The page date shown is January 28, 2026.
chipset_scope: A15 or later; M2 or later (as stated)
limitations: The support table's cells are images in the fetched copy. A17 Pro is not named in the text. Documentation-level statement only; not a statement about any build.

title: Apple's Platform Security guide states that Memory Integrity Enforcement is available on A19 and M5 processors or later
description: The MIE passage of the same guide names A19 and M5 processors or later. The A17 family is not named in that passage.
chipset_scope: A19 and M5 or later (as stated)
limitations: A negative inference for A17 (see C-012) is drawn from the stated scope and is not a direct statement that the A17 Pro lacks the hardware.

title: The A15-A18 column of the Platform Security guide's feature table includes the A17 generation; the support cells are not readable from the fetched copy
description: The feature table has a column headed A15-A18. The cells are images in the fetched copy, so the support marks in that column cannot be read from the text.
limitations: Refines the limitation of C-013 for range-based reading. Support marks for the A17 column are not established by the text.
